subject: English
question_text: ‘Pakistan was finally behind him’ ⎯⎯ Explain.
guide_solution: Bangabandhu got released from Pakistani custody after nine months captivity. Then in the evening of 7 Jnuary 1972, he boarded on a London bound P\A aircraft from chuklala Airport in Rawalpindi a part of his home return. And, no sooner had the aircraft taken off than Pakistan was finally behind him.
source: SSC English 1st-paper Udayan Secondary School, Barishal (Test Paper School) 2023

question_text: “In fact, his name and independence became synonymous” ⎯⎯ explain.
guide_solution: The expression refers to the fact that the independence of Bangladesh cannot be imagined without Bangabandhu. Bangabandhu declared the independence of Bangladesh, inspired the Bangalees to fight against the Pakistan Army and guided to victory.

subject: English
question_text: Why do you think a grave was dug just in front of Bangabandhu’s prison cell?
guide_solution: While in the prison Bangabandhu was fearless and so bold. Because he knew that nothing would stop the Bangalees to gain independence. This belief about the Bangalees made him so bold in the prison. And to restrain or dishearten Bangabandhu, the cowardly Pakistani dug a grave just in front of Bangabandhu's prison cell.
source: SSC English 1st-paper Udayan Secondary School, Barishal (Test Paper School) 2023
